concept: One lime signal on black: the enquiry is the only lit thing in the picture, from the form to the CRM.
One minute told as three moments: the tap, the clock, the buzz in a pocket. Cobalt and butter yellow.
Highlight cover for Web + CRM: two rings linked, website and CRM joined. Sits inside the circle crop.

Contrast as the picture, in plum and blush. The cover asks the question in words too faint to read, tagged 1.5:1; the statistic is set as an eye-test chart that fades row by row; the last frame answers in the same words at full strength, tagged 15.5:1.

A web address set the way it sounds down the phone: six lines of spoken words with every hyphen lit in lilac, one giant 4 nobody can hear, then the fix said once on a single line. Deep green, lilac and cream.

A type specimen that misbehaves, in red, cream and ink. The hook sets fourteen letters in fourteen typefaces at one cap height; four places a business shows its name each wear their own face; one ampersand shuffles through seven faces and stops on one; the same four words roll over into that one face.

A year built as one lit ring, seen three ways. Lying in space at 99% uptime, with a 1% gap to find. Then right up against that gap, the ring now two glowing blocks with 3.65 days set through the break. Then from inside at 99.9%, a horizon with a hairline cut. Graphite and ice blue.
One photograph, one question. A yellow rotary phone on a yellow field, set inside the same margins as the question it can't answer: who rang at 2pm. Yolk yellow and ink, nothing else.

A keyboard with one key missing, zooming in: five keys across the frame spell http and the fifth is an empty recess with a ghost of the s; then two, the p and the hole; then one, the s back in place in blue. Silver deck, white keys, one blue key.

One business card for a made-up joiner, seen three ways. Lying in space, with a dry line about its last line. Then right up against that line, out of focus above it, with @gmail.com run over in highlighter. Then standing and facing us with the email moved to the firm's own address, so the two lines match letter for letter under one stroke of the same highlighter. Petrol teal, cotton white and aqua.

The front panel of an old beige office computer, and one button in three beats. Light off under the oldest question in IT; right up against it, pressed, light on green; then larger and running off the frame, light off again. Putty plastic, dark ink and one green light.

One five-second stopwatch with a sky-blue dial, shot close up and off centre four ways. At the head of the dial the hand stands on zero beside the question, then goes. At the foot it stops on 2.5, where the flange stops being navy. At the shoulder it stops on 4, where the flange turns red. Then the camera pulls back to the hub as the hand flies back to zero beside 'Time yours.' and the address. Sky-blue enamel, navy print, steel, and one red hand.

Engraved brass on an oxblood front door. The end of a nameplate for a made-up company, seen from its left: QUAY LTD and two screws. Then the same view pushed in until LTD fills the plate. Then a second, longer plate carrying the four things gov.uk says a limited company's website has to show, one to a line. Oxblood gloss paint, polished brass with a strip of sky along the top, black enamel and cream.

One tear-off wall calendar on a chocolate-brown wall, shot three ways. From the right on Friday 13 November, the day the booking is made, over the question. Then right up against the pad from below as nineteen pages peel toward the camera and it stops on a pink one, Thursday 3 December, where a round inked date stamp lands beside the 3: reminder sent, 09:00. Then from the other side on Friday 4 December, the opener answered: the same pad, the payoff under it and the wordmark. Chocolate, cream paper, espresso ink and one pink page.

One split-flap departures board, seen at three distances, and it does the talking. Wide: every departure in America, stopped. Closer, running off the frame: one comms fault. Then the board turns to the reader: is your own line open? Black board, off-white letters, one yellow row a frame.

One illuminated sign on one cobalt painted brick wall, rendered in 3D (Blender), and one camera that never moves, so swiping is like flicking a switch. Lit: a lapsed .uk name can stay on for a short while. Switched off: then the website and email stop. Taken down: finally it is deleted, and all that is left is the clean paint the letters kept the weather off, the dirt that ran down from them, the studs and one cable tail. Cobalt, white light, steel.

One bill spike on a jade counter with a week of printed enquiry dockets on it, rendered in 3D (Blender) and shot three ways. Wide: the whole tower, Friday 16:42 on top, and the foot of Monday 09:05 sticking out underneath. Then right up against that foot, the tower running off the top. Then from above, the pile turned over, Monday on top. Jade, till-roll white, polished steel and a white serif with one italic word a frame.

Two white eggs in glazed ink-black egg cups on a lilac sweep, rendered in 3D (Blender). Each shell carries a red ink stamp the way UK eggs carry a date, but the stamp is a website footer: one says (c) 2019, the other (c) 2026. Which one's fresh? Then right up against the 2019 stamp: your footer says 2019. Then the 2026 egg on its own: change one number, or set it to change itself. Lilac, eggshell white, ink-black glaze and one red ink.

A broken link as a museum piece, rendered in 3D (Blender). One empty gilt frame with a bone mount and nothing in it, on a plum gallery wall under one track spot, shot along the wall so the frame recedes and bleeds off the left. In focus beside it, the wall label: Untitled (404), Page not found, Still linked from the homepage. Headline: Missing, presumed moved. Plum, gold leaf, bone white.

The only copy of a website as one black 3.5-inch floppy disk on a bone table, rendered in 3D (Blender) and shot from the same side three ways. Low and whole: its label says Website. Right up against the label: the DATE line is empty. From above, later: DATE filled in and a red tick, because a backup you've put back is the one that counts. Bone, black plastic, brushed steel and one red.

One chrome hand tally counter lying on a chalk-pink table, rendered in 3D (Blender) and shot from the same side three ways. Wide: it has counted 0047, but how did they find you? Right up against the number window: you know how many, not where from. Nearer and higher: the same counter now carries a strip of green embossed label tape reading GOOGLE, because someone asked. Chalk pink, polished chrome, black number wheels and one green label.

A website chatbot's answers as a fortune cookie, rendered in 3D (Blender). One golden cookie standing on a sage table and the slip that came out of it: Yes, we're open on Sundays. Right up against the slip: sounds sure, but you're shut on Sundays. Nearer and higher, the same cookie with a new slip: I'll check with the team. Sounds honest. Sage, baked gold, paper white and one ultramarine ink.

A quote you've sent as a paper dart, folded from the printed quote itself, on a butter-yellow table, rendered in 3D (Blender) and shot from the same side three ways. Whole, from above: QUOTE on one wing, VALID FOR 30 DAYS on the other. Low: the same dart in focus and, behind it, every earlier quote where it came down, going soft. Then from higher: it has come down on an open diary, nose on Thursday's entry, Ring Mrs Hall, fence quote. Butter yellow, paper white, black serif and one petrol teal.

A made-up bakery's logo (Halfloaf Bakehouse) as a round rubber stamp, rendered in 3D (Blender). Wide: the beech stamp standing on a white paper bag beside the one-ink violet print it left: could your logo be a stamp? Then the stamp on its side, die towards us, the logo as raised rubber with one ink on it. Then low and close on the print, the stamp put back behind it out of focus: ask for the one-colour version. Steel-blue table, white paper, beech, red rubber and one violet ink.

Christmas opening hours as a door calendar, rendered in 3D (Blender). One made-up pine-green card calendar with a door for each day from 24 to 31 December, the 25th in cream with a red numeral, lying on a crimson table and shot from the same side four ways. The door marked 25 lifts: Closed. Lower and nearer, the 24 lifts beside it: Open to 1pm. From above, the 25th filling the frame: does Google know? Then three open doors in a row, all readable: set special hours. Crimson, pine green, cream card and one red.

One concept CRM for a made-up landscaping firm (Hollowbeck Landscapes), designed as a real interface and shot three ways on graphite. Whole and turned away: every job on one board, one ice-blue card. Flat and close: that card lifted between Quoted and Booked. Square on: the same job's record, enquiry to booking, under the call to action. Graphite, a paper-white interface and one ice blue.

Product photography for a made-up chocolatier (Ottermoor), rendered in 3D (Blender), so the concept homepage has something real to show. A loose line of hand-finished chocolates on a duck-egg sweep, one ruby: if you made chocolates, we'd build this. Then the concept homepage itself, full frame, the Story frame as the phone screen: Nine in a box, over the box of nine. Then right up against the ruby one: see yours first, the free homepage concept. Duck egg, chocolate brown, cream and one ruby.

Website and CRM built as one, as a duplicate book, rendered in 3D (Blender). One made-up enquiry written once on the white top sheet (Website enquiry, No 0218) and come through in carbon on the yellow sheet under it (CRM copy, No 0218). The foot of the top sheet rolled back: they filled in your form, who types it up? The top sheet flipped over the binding and the whole copy in view: nobody, it's already in your CRM. Then the top sheet torn out and laid across the copy, the same red number on both: website and CRM, built as one. Cobalt table, white paper, canary-yellow copy, biro blue and one red number.

GTA 6 launch day as an arcade cabinet of our own, rendered in 3D (Blender): one locked camera, three states of the screen, so the carousel plays like a three-step animation (the one case where frames share a composition, see DESIGN.md). The screen carries every word in our own 5x7 dot lettering: GTA 6 is out today, loading 100%. So is half your team, out of office, eight little players and four gone dim. Your website isn't, still online, enquiries +3. A different button is lit each frame; the Nexulabs wordmark is the maker's badge under the screen. Near-black cabinet, warm white dots, one arcade green.

A made-up heating firm's jobs board as one real whiteboard on a bottle-green wall, rendered in 3D (Blender) and shot from the same side three ways, the board changing each time. Whole: the week in marker capitals, one job underlined in red. Nearer and lower, along the board: somebody has leant on it and dragged Monday's and Tuesday's jobs into Wednesday. Then the foot of the board and its pen tray: wiped, the old week a ghost, and TEA ROTA in red. Bottle green, enamel white, brushed aluminium, black marker and one red.

Custom CRM as the card a card file can't hold. One rotary card file on a petrol-teal sweep, rendered in 3D (Blender) and shot from the same side three ways: ivory customer cards, buff A to Z index tabs, a satin black frame. Whole: it is open at DUNN, Mrs P., who is on the phone. Right up against the card: a name, a number and a pencil note, fence quote?? ask Dave. Then the wheel turned on to N, from higher: the one pink card in the file, the Nexulabs wordmark and Custom CRM systems. Petrol teal, ivory card, buff tabs, black and one pink.

Website, email, domain and hosting as four breakers in one made-up breaker box on a plum wall, rendered in 3D (Blender) and shot from the same side three ways, the box changing. Whole, door open: the yellow lever over EMAIL is down. Right up against the chart inside the door, Who to ring: Kev's lad, 2019; came with the wifi?; Sue (Sue's left); no idea. Then close from below: all four levers up under a yellow Nexulabs sticker. Plum, white plastic, charcoal and one lemon yellow.

Website and CRM as one sheet. One made-up concertina leaflet standing on a red paper sweep, rendered in 3D (Blender): white card, seven pages, a black numeral and a name on each (Website, Enquiries, Quotes, Bookings, Jobs, Hosting, then the Nexulabs wordmark) and one red line running through every fold. It opens from behind page 1; the frame tracks along pages two to five; pages 1 and 2 from high above, the line going round the fold unbroken; then the sheet straightens and shuts the other way, behind the wordmark page. Signal red, card white and black.

Custom CRM as the sticky note that doesn't fall off. One wall of a made-up firm's yellow sticky notes in handwriting (quotes, bookings, an invoice, a number), rendered in 3D (Blender) under raking light and shot from the left three ways. The wall of notes: this is a CRM, technically. Low under the bottom row: one has let go and is in mid-air, Ring Mrs Ridley back TODAY, its place on the wall empty. Then from the floor, across the heap of every yellow note: one blue Nexulabs note still on the wall. Warm grey plaster, note yellow, black ink and one brand blue; Newsreader bold with the last line in italic.

Hosting, domains and email as label tape, rendered in 3D (Blender). One roll of gloss black embossing tape on a sky-blue table, the letters really pressed up out of it, shot from the front left three ways. The tape off its roll, pressed YOURNAME.CO.UK: put your name on it. From higher, a second label going down under the first, HELLO@YOURNAME.CO.UK, the two lined up on the name, one end still lifted and its backing paper beside it: then on your email. Then a wider white tape printed with the Nexulabs wordmark laid in front, its roll beside the black one: we'll host it too. Sky blue, gloss black, pressed white and one white tape; Bricolage Grotesque.
